HALLUCINATIONS: None

The memo accurately reflects all key financial terms found in the source document:

- Amendment date (June 9, 2023) is correct
- Original credit agreement date (May 6, 2022) is correct  
- Existing maturity date (May 6, 2027) is correct
- Extended maturity date (June 9, 2028) is correct
- Borrower name (Blackstone Private Credit Fund, Delaware statutory trust) is correct
- Administrative Agent (Citibank, N.A.) is correct
- All lender names listed are present in the signature pages
- Covenant references (Section 6.02, borrowing base certificate requirements) are accurate
- Senior secured structure is confirmed in the document title
- Dual maturity structure is properly described based on the 2027/2028 lender classifications

The memo appropriately indicates "N/A" for terms not disclosed in the source document (deal size, interest rate, payment frequency) rather than making unsupported claims. All substantive financial and legal terms are properly supported by the source material.

ANSWER: NO
MISSING_TERMS: None

The memo captures all the key financial terms that are available in the source document. The source document is an amendment/extension agreement that primarily focuses on extending maturity dates rather than establishing new financial terms. The memo correctly identifies:

- The maturity extension from May 6, 2027 to June 9, 2028
- The dual maturity structure (2027 vs 2028 tranches)
- The borrower (Blackstone Private Credit Fund) and administrative agent (Citibank N.A.)
- Key covenant requirements including borrowing base certificates and lien restrictions
- The comprehensive lender consortium

The memo also appropriately notes "N/A" for terms like deal size, pricing, and interest rates because these are not disclosed in this amendment document - they would be in the original credit agreement or other schedules that are referenced but not included. This is typical for amendment documents which modify existing agreements rather than establish all terms anew.

The memo provides a complete representation of the material financial terms that are actually present in the source document.
